authority: These are optional curriculum lines. They do not change the 64-module universal core, grant operating authority, or authorize a credential or release.
entryRule: The universal core has no programming prerequisite. A readiness diagnostic, prior evidence, or instructor review determines entry to Builder Bridge and Advanced Agent Systems studios.

programs.title: One Water AI Builder Bridge
programs.promise: Give a motivated non-programmer or early builder enough technical understanding to read, change, test, connect, release, and defend a small governed utility application.
audience: curious leaders who want hands-on depth
programs.completionProduct: reproducible read-only utility application and release evidence package

modules.title: Python and Computational Thinking for Utility Work
modules.learningJob: Read and explain a small program, break a utility task into clear steps, make a bounded change, run it, inspect the result, and correct an error without pretending code is self-explanatory.
outcomes: Explain variables, values, conditions, loops, functions, classes, imports, and errors in plain English.
Break a utility record-processing task into inputs, rules, transformations, outputs, checks, and failure handling.
Read unfamiliar Python before changing it and predict the effect of a proposed change.
Run, test, debug, and document a small approved-data program.
Create a Python task map and tested script evidence record.
modules.appliedResult: Python task map and tested script evidence record

modules.title: Data Structures, Files, and Application Data
modules.learningJob: Work with tables, lists, dictionaries, JavaScript Object Notation, files, dates, missing values, and identifiers while preserving the meaning, source, and limitation of utility records.
outcomes: Distinguish a value, field, row, table, list, dictionary, object, file, record, and relationship.
Read and write comma-separated values and JavaScript Object Notation without silently changing types or identifiers.
Inspect missing, duplicate, conflicting, stale, and malformed data before using it.
Preserve source, version, time, units, and transformation evidence.
Create a governed application-data contract and validation log.
modules.appliedResult: governed application-data contract and validation log

modules.title: Application Programming Interfaces, Hypertext Transfer Protocol, and Tool Connections
modules.learningJob: Trace a governed request from an authenticated user through an application programming interface to an approved system, then inspect the response, error, permission, rate, and log.
outcomes: Explain endpoint, request, method, header, body, response, status code, authentication, rate limit, and timeout.
Compare a direct application programming interface, connector, webhook, and Model Context Protocol tool connection.
Design the narrowest useful read-only permission for a utility task.
Handle failure, retry, timeout, duplicate request, and human escalation without hiding the error.
Create a governed tool-connection contract and request log.
modules.appliedResult: governed tool-connection contract and request log

modules.title: Git, GitHub, and Reproducible Work
modules.learningJob: Use version control to preserve who changed what, why it changed, how it was reviewed, what evidence passed, and how a weak change can be reversed.
outcomes: Explain repository, working tree, branch, commit, difference, merge, conflict, tag, issue, and pull request.
Create a branch and commit that preserves one bounded curriculum or application change.
Review a difference, connect it to an issue and acceptance rule, and record reviewer action.
Resolve a simple conflict without erasing either contributor's work or history.
Create a reproducible change and review record.

modules.title: Testing, Dependencies, and Environments
modules.learningJob: Prove that a change works under known conditions, fails visibly under wrong conditions, and can be reproduced outside the builder's laptop.
outcomes: Distinguish unit, integration, regression, security, accessibility, and acceptance tests.
Identify code, package, version, configuration, secret, operating system, and service dependencies.
Create and use an isolated environment with recorded dependency versions.
Design tests for ordinary, boundary, malformed, unauthorized, and failure cases.
Create a test, dependency, and environment evidence package.
modules.appliedResult: test, dependency, and environment evidence package

modules.title: Cloud Foundations, Identity, Secrets, and Cost
modules.learningJob: Explain and configure the smallest supportable hosted application while keeping identity, permission, data, secrets, logs, cost, resilience, and exit visible.
outcomes: Explain region, network, compute, storage, database, identity, secret, log, domain, certificate, backup, and managed service.
Trace user, application, model, tool, data, and log flows across a cloud architecture.
Set least-privilege identity, secret rotation, spend caps, logging, backup, and recovery responsibilities.
Compare hosted, local, managed, and hybrid patterns without assuming one is always safer or cheaper.
Create a cloud responsibility, cost, and recovery map.
modules.appliedResult: cloud responsibility, cost, and recovery map
prerequisites: bridge:BB03 and bridge:BB05 or equivalent evidence

modules.title: Continuous Integration, Delivery, and Release Control
modules.learningJob: Move an approved change through automated checks, artifact creation, environment promotion, human approval, release, observation, and rollback.
outcomes: Distinguish continuous integration, continuous delivery, continuous deployment, release, and environment promotion.
Design an automated pipeline that fails closed when required evidence is missing.
Connect tests, artifact checksums, approvals, release notes, deployment, monitoring, and rollback.
Investigate a failed release and preserve the prior working state and incident evidence.
Create a continuous delivery and release-control record.
prerequisites: bridge:BB04 through bridge:BB06 or equivalent evidence

modules.title: Builder Readiness Practicum
modules.learningJob: Bring code, data, tools, version control, tests, cloud responsibility, and release evidence together in a small read-only utility application that another person can reproduce and review.
outcomes: Define a bounded utility problem, user, approved source, non-goals, and acceptance evidence.
Build a read-only application that preserves source, identity, permission, error, and log boundaries.
Use a reviewed repository, tests, dependency lock, environment record, and controlled deployment path.
Demonstrate one ordinary case, one failure case, one recovery, and one rollback.
Defend the reproducible application and release evidence package to a technical and utility reviewer.
modules.appliedResult: reproducible read-only utility application and release evidence package
prerequisites: bridge:BB01 through bridge:BB07 or approved equivalent evidence

programs.title: One Water AI Advanced Agent Systems
programs.promise: Give technical practitioners and reviewers a governed path through formal agent design, planning, retrieval, memory, multi-agent coordination, human interaction, learning methods, and embodied systems in water-sector settings.
programs.completionProduct: advanced utility agent-system architecture, evaluation, and authority portfolio

modules.title: Agents, Goals, Environments, and Perceived Agency
modules.learningJob: Specify what an agent is trying to achieve, what it can observe and do, how the environment changes, how success is measured, and why people may perceive more agency than the system has.
outcomes: Compare rational-agent, language-model agent, workflow, and human-team descriptions.
Specify performance, environment, observations, actions, state, tools, and stop conditions.
Analyze observability, uncertainty, change, reversibility, and consequence in a utility environment.
Identify anthropomorphic language and interface cues that distort trust and authority.
Create an advanced agent environment and authority model.
modules.appliedResult: advanced agent environment and authority model
prerequisites: fellowship:M17 through fellowship:M24 or approved equivalent evidence

modules.title: Planning, Reasoning, Tool Use, and Stop Conditions
modules.learningJob: Compare planning patterns, inspect observable reasoning and action traces, control tool use, detect plan drift, and stop when evidence or authority fails.
outcomes: Compare fixed workflow, classical planning, language-model planning, plan-and-execute, Reason and Act, and reflection.
Trace goal, plan, action, observation, evidence, evaluation, adjustment, and stop.
Set tool permissions, retry budgets, time and cost limits, escalation, and refusal.
Diagnose plan drift, tool misuse, endless loops, stale evidence, and false completion.
Create and test an advanced planning and stop-control specification.

modules.title: Agentic Retrieval and Evidence-Grounded Research
modules.learningJob: Build an iterative research and retrieval process that plans questions, selects approved sources, retrieves evidence, evaluates coverage, refines the search, and preserves conflicts and limitations.
outcomes: Distinguish ordinary search, retrieval-augmented generation, graph-assisted retrieval, and agentic retrieval.
Plan a research question into source, claim, locator, conflict, and stopping requirements.
Evaluate source coverage, freshness, authority, duplication, conflict, and unsupported synthesis.
Control internet, repository, document, and database tool use while preserving permissions and citations.
Create an agentic research plan, trace, claim register, and evidence package.
modules.appliedResult: agentic research plan, trace, claim register, and evidence package

modules.title: Memory, State, Durable Records, and Correction
modules.learningJob: Separate temporary context, working state, episodic and semantic memory, learned parameters, and authoritative records so the system remembers only what it may keep and corrects history without erasing it.
outcomes: Distinguish context, working state, cache, memory, retrieval source, model weights, and system of record.
Design retention, access, provenance, correction, deletion, expiration, and conflict rules.
Identify memory poisoning, stale state, cross-user leakage, false personalization, and record-authority failures.
Use checkpoints and append-only corrections to preserve task and decision history.
Create an agent state, memory, and authoritative-record plan.
modules.appliedResult: agent state, memory, and authoritative-record plan

modules.title: Multi-Agent Coordination, Conflict, and Failure
modules.learningJob: Design and test a multi-agent work system that preserves roles, evidence, communication, shared state, disagreement, arbitration, cost, failure recovery, and human command.
outcomes: Compare supervisor, hierarchy, peer, market, blackboard, and sequential handoff coordination patterns.
Design agent roles, messages, state, source versions, permissions, arbitration, escalation, and final human decision.
Use basic cooperation and incentive reasoning to expose conflict and gaming without personifying agents.
Trigger and recover from disagreement, deadlock, duplicate work, cascading error, and cost multiplication.
Create a tested multi-agent coordination, evaluation, and recovery package.
modules.appliedResult: tested multi-agent coordination, evaluation, and recovery package

modules.title: Human-Agent Interaction and Agentic User Experience
modules.learningJob: Design a usable and accessible interaction in which a person can understand status and evidence, control consequential action, challenge the system, interrupt it, correct it, recover, and retain authority.
outcomes: Explain trust calibration, common ground, transparency, progressive disclosure, feedback, and recoverability.
Design visible goal, plan, source, tool, state, limitation, cost, and next-action behavior.
Create preview, confirmation, interrupt, cancel, pause, correction, undo, recovery, and escalation states.
Evaluate automation bias, inaccessible controls, hidden state, false confidence, dark patterns, and weak handoffs.
Create and test an accessible agentic user-experience and recovery specification.
modules.appliedResult: accessible agentic user-experience and recovery specification

modules.title: Reinforcement, Feedback, and Continual Learning
modules.learningJob: Explain how systems change from feedback, examples, rewards, fine-tuning, memory, retrieval, and software updates, then decide which forms of change are permitted and reviewed in a utility setting.
outcomes: Distinguish prompt revision, retrieval update, memory, supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, reinforcement learning, and continual learning.
Explain state, action, reward, policy, exploration, exploitation, and delayed consequence with a bounded example.
Identify reward misspecification, unsafe exploration, feedback contamination, policy drift, and unreviewed self-change.
Design offline, simulated, shadow, advisory, and controlled review stages before any physical-system use.
Create a learning-method decision and safety record.

modules.title: Embodied Artificial Intelligence and Water Robotics
modules.learningJob: Evaluate how sensing, perception, language, planning, simulation, robotics, deterministic control, and human authority connect when an artificial intelligence system affects the physical world.
outcomes: Distinguish software agent, simulated agent, embodied agent, robot, vision-language-action model, deterministic controller, and qualified operator.
Trace sensor, perception, model, plan, command, control, actuator, physical response, feedback, and human intervention.
Evaluate inspection, sampling, laboratory, maintenance, field, and treatment-support scenarios for consequence and reversibility.
Design simulation, shadow, read-only, advisory, interlock, emergency-stop, and human-approval boundaries.
Create an embodied-system evidence, control, and authority case.
modules.appliedResult: embodied-system evidence, control, and authority case
